business: Mama Fit (online postpartum home strength program; profile is a guess until interviews are done)
by_segment: Back at work, baby in care
Mum of two or more, stretched for time
why_not: I'd probably start the free 5 weeks in a burst of motivation, but 45 minutes a day while back at work with a baby won't last, and I'd drop off long before I'd need to pay for the 8-week program. Plus there are free postpartum workouts on YouTube if I get keen again.

I'd sign up for the free 5 weeks, but honestly I'll do it a couple of times then drift. I'm a class person, I turn up because the other mums are there, not because a video is waiting on my phone. 45 minutes a day at home with two kids just isn't happening.

I'd try the free 5 weeks, but I'm leaking when I sneeze, so I want a women's health physio telling me what to do, not a program from a mum on Instagram. 45 minutes a day of 3x10 also isn't going to fit around work and a baby.

It's made by a mum of three, not a women's health physio, and nothing says anyone qualified designed or checked it. With my diastasis and pelvic floor I'd rather spend the money on a physio session and do what she gives me, and 45 minutes a day of 3x10 sounds like a lot for someone still healing.

45 minutes a day just isn't real for me when the baby naps for 30 minutes on a good day. I might tap into the free 5 weeks, but I'd probably drop off and go back to free YouTube rather than pay for the next bit.

I'd probably grab the free 5 weeks in a burst of motivation, but 45 minutes a day with a full-time job and a baby isn't happening, and I'd drop off well before I ever got to the paid part. Twenty bucks isn't the issue, the time is.

I already pay every month for a big fitness app that has a postpartum plan, so I don't need another one. I might try the free 5 weeks out of curiosity, but that's 5 weeks of free stuff before I'd even think about paying, and I'd probably stop there.

I'd definitely sign up for the free 5 weeks from my feed during a night feed, but that's a month of content right there and I'm not paying for the next bit until I've actually finished it. Honestly, with a newborn, 45 minutes a day is a stretch and I'd probably still be on week 2 or 3 at the end of the month.
